title: Bur
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Somalia's own filled fried pastry, its half-moon shape and thicker, more pliable dough setting it apart from the crisp, sharp-cornered sambuusa, typically filled with spiced meat or vegetables.
longDesc: Bur and sambuusa are often confused by outsiders, but Somali cooks distinguish them clearly - bur uses a softer, more bread-like dough folded into a half-moon rather than sambuusa's thin, crisp pastry folded into a tight triangle, giving bur a chewier, more substantial bite.
ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying
300 g (10.5 oz) cooked, spiced ground meat filling (as for Sambuusa)
steps: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and let sit for 10 minutes.
Combine the flour and salt, then add the yeast mixture and oil, kneading into a smooth, soft dough.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each out into a round about 12cm across.
Place a spoonful of the meat filling on one half of each round.
Fold over into a half-moon shape, pressing the edges firmly to seal.
Fry the bur in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
chefTips: Bur dough is softer and more yeasted than sambuusa thin pastry wrapper, giving it a distinctly chewier bite.
Seal the edges firmly, crimping if needed, to prevent the filling from leaking during frying.
These are best served warm, shortly after frying.
commonMistakes: Rolling the dough too thin, losing bur characteristic softer, more substantial texture.
Not sealing the edges well enough, allowing the filling to escape into the oil.
Overfilling, which makes the pastries difficult to seal properly.
storage: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate leftovers for up to 1 day.
reheating: Reheat in a hot oven to help re-crisp.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the meat filling, best enjoyed as an occasional treat given the frying.
culturalNote: Bur is a distinct cousin to sambuusa in Somali cooking, its softer, yeasted dough giving it a different character prized in its own right rather than as a simple variation.
